data.evidence: cell_tower on minizinc_gecode was rejected as invalid_solution in run breadth2-20260915. The cause is MiniZinc 2.9.3 flattening: with the reference's one-sided coverage bound, the budget constraint compiled to int_lin_le([3,4],[build_tower[1],covered[2]],4) and build_tower[2] appeared in no constraint at all, so the runner reported a solution spending 7 against a budget of 4. MiniZinc's own output item calls that solution infeasible and Chuffed reproduces it. Stating the bound as an equivalence flattens soundly, which tests/minizinc_gecode_flattening_regression.py demonstrates through the evaluator.
